key_insight: Accordion lets one mixture-of-experts language model serve five inference budgets by repeatedly executing fixed layer prefixes, improving performance as inference depth increases.
engineering_relevance: A single shared-parameter model can offer multiple compute–quality settings, reducing the need to train and maintain separate models for different inference budgets.
method: Define five execution paths using fixed-prefix layer looping, with an unlooped minimum-budget path.
Jointly pretrain by sampling one budget per micro-batch and optimizing next-token prediction without cross-budget consistency losses.
Preserve all budgets through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, integrating three domain experts via parameter-group merging and budget-matched multi-teacher on-policy distillation.
evidence_signal: After 3.6T pretraining tokens, increased depth improved the five-category macro-average across 37 tasks by 3.01 percentage points; the middle budget captured 89% of that gain with half as many additional layer executions.
watch_item: Layer-execution counts are not direct latency measurements; deployment benefits require hardware-specific profiling of looping and mixture-of-experts routing.
paper_title: Accordion: Elastic-Depth Inference via Fixed-Prefix Layer Looping
